results.statement: sc-lint's PORT-010 (sc-lint's rule that reports a production #[cfg(unix)] item lacking a #[cfg(windows)] companion or portable fallback) changes must not blanket-suppress real parity gaps: a production #[cfg(unix)] item with no #[cfg(windows)] companion and no portable fallback must still be reported.
results.quote:
REQ-PRODUCT-004AA/PORT-010 (docs/requirements.md): "`PORT-010` - production structural `#[cfg(unix)]` companion-parity checks"

ADR-010 decision 6 (Accepted): "Explicit `#[cfg(unix)]` production boundaries are treated as structural parity questions for the shared portability family. Leaf rules may suppress inside those items, with the companion-or-fallback decision owned by the structural parity rule family instead of parallel per-rule allowlists."

Issue #786 (atm-core verdict table, 2026-10-30): "#720 covers only the crate-root main.rs shape; this issue tracks the complete remaining inventory and asks for per-case classification, not blanket suppression of real parity gaps."
results.context: Phase M v3: requirement/ADR-based derivation under ADR-022 direction, 2026-10-30; candidate P9

criteria.no: The item is about a different part of the system or a different activity, and completing it would neither follow nor break the anchor.
criteria.unclear: The item text is too vague to tell what part of the system it touches.
criteria.yes: The item plans, changes, or depends on the thing the anchor statement is about, directly or as a clear prerequisite.

relevant.instructions: The state holds one planning item (`item.title`, `item.text`) and one anchor: a directive the user stated verbatim in `anchor.statement`, with the area it governs in `anchor.scope`. Does the work described in `item.text` touch the subject that `anchor.statement` talks about? Judge overlap of subject matter only. Do not judge whether the item obeys the anchor.

criteria.no: The item does not say so, or it suppresses such items broadly.
criteria.unclear: The item mentions this in wording that cannot be read either way.
criteria.yes: The item explicitly says real gaps (unpaired, unannotated or negative-case items) are still reported.

addressed.instructions: `anchor.statement` requires that a production #[cfg(unix)] item with no #[cfg(windows)] companion and no portable fallback still be reported. Does `item.text` explicitly keep that, for example by saying unpaired or unannotated items or negative cases stay reported? A plan that suppresses many items at once does not keep it. Judge presence only.

criteria.no: The item plans no blanket suppression.
criteria.unclear: The item plans a suppression whose reach cannot be told.
criteria.yes: The item plans such a blanket suppression.

contradicted.instructions: Does `item.text` plan a blanket suppression of PORT-010 findings: skipping #[cfg(unix)] items by file, module, path, crate, name pattern or a switch, regardless of whether each has a companion, a portable fallback or its own per-site allowance? Not blanket suppression: recognising a specific companion shape (for example a same-name #[cfg(not(unix))] sibling), honouring a reasoned allowance on one annotated item, silence, or unrelated work. Judge conflict only.

results.explanation: This bead proposes something the anchor rules out.
